questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Spanish is my second language and I wanted to practice my academic spanish and my psanish in general.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The fact that the courses are in spanish.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: it's a very different experience from my home university. The teaching was a lot of rote learning and almost all the exams where in hand, and not on a computer.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: it was okay easy. They send me some emails with the information on where to go.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: we had to diferent introduction days. One in general and one at our specific campus. The one at the campus came with introductions to student organizations.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I don't know how easy it was. I found some other people going on exchange in Madrid by making a post on a facebook group called Madrid International Students. A lot of people use Idealista. You just have to be aware, because there is a lot of scam housings on idealista. I Recomend to find a housing where someone is already living, so you don't have to pay a real estate agent for crazy high fees

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is chill. Campus is very far away and there is no housing on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I don't know what is meant by housing availabe to students...

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: it was all through mobility online and the host university send me the information needed directly to my email.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to register before arriving. If by registration you mean to have acces to the university website and stuff like that it is as descirbed before. They send you the information to your email. If you mean how esay it was to sign your paper of arrival at the university, I did it through Mobility Online, but a lot of people went to the erasmus office to get their documents signed. Complutense de Madrid have erasmus offices on every campus to help echange students.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: personal help, help via email and help through phonecall.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: okay succesful. Some of the courses I wanted were not available for exchange students, but it wasn't stated on their website. But the process upon arrival was easy. You can change your courses during the first couple of weeks of the semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: follow the instructions in the email.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: again, maybe it was just very different from what I am used to. a lot of rote learning and multiple choice exams. Not very focused on theory and analysis

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took Ba courses. I don't know how much more I can elaborate on this...

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think the style of teaching in some ways is very similar. You have a small classroom of people and the professor speaks from a powerpoint presentation. Sometimes they ask questions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
* Relaciones Internacionales e integración en America Latina
* Regimen Internacional del medio ambiente
* Geografía Política
* Sociología de las Migraciones

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Sociología de las Migraciones. I would recommend this course because the professor is very good and kind. The professor, BERTA ALVAREZ-MIRANDA NAVARRO, makes the teaching interesting and it is very debate-oriented, which makes it nice compared to the listening oriented teaching of a lot of other courses.

Also Geografía Política with Sergio is a nice course. Just beware that there's a good amount of homework consisting of 5-page essays.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: no unexpected costs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: compared to Denmark almost everything was cheaper. Maybe Onions and avocados were more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not use any, but there were a lot of opportunities to do so

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: everything from chess-club to movie clubs, to every sport imaginable.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I don't know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend you check with ESN. European Student Network. They host a lot of weekend tours. I didn't go on any myself, but a lot of friends went, and have recommended it.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy for me, but I also speak the language.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: it is difficult. They already have their established friend groups and will not go out of their way to include you. I almost only spoke with local students in class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: they eat late in spain - the daily rutine is long. You wake up early and go to bed late, so you will be tired a lot.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the food and the relaxed feeling of not everything has to go fast.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't be so afraid of the attendance registration at the university. I think it applies mostly to local students. It made it difficult to go on tours, so I didn't see a lot of Spain. Speak direclty with your professors and ask them if it is okay you miss some classes.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: really, even if it is spam and sometimes annoying; Join the ESN WhatsApp group. A lot of things happen in Madrid so it's nice that someone is giving you the information.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: meeting a lot of international people and becoming friends with people from all around the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: having to attend at the university all the time. I'm used to free studyprograms, so it is not required to attend at UCPH, but it is at Complutense de Madrid. Spend a lot more time on campus than I would have liked.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
